# Format: <hint><TAB><member CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY member case fails)
# First line doubles as the foothold; lines are ordered most-fundamental first.

How is a number written in an arbitrary base: what does a symbol's place in the output stand for, and what does the base's length say about it? For a negative number, what must come out before the digits?

Before converting anything, when is a base even usable? Think about its length, whether the same symbol appears twice, and whether a sign character could collide with the '-' you print for negatives. What should the function do when the base fails these checks?
When the number is zero, what single symbol should come out? Is it always a hard-coded zero digit, or is it whatever symbol sits first in the given base?

The most negative int has no positive counterpart in an int. Which of these rows fail, and does anything your code computes on the way to its digits need a value its type cannot hold on some platform? (What C promises about the width of each type: docs/testing.md, under ilp32.)
